scope: One combined initial review of the three whole tasks, original images, native TikZ semantics, solutions, classifications, taught/prior context, method minimum and individual ratings. minimumSelection.rationale: All three are needed to represent the distinct whole demands within this scoped minimum: cosine requires relating a tangent through the origin to a global comparison at a different point on its selected lobe; logarithm bounds both local tangent coefficients from an interval; the multipart graph question combines transformation recognition with reading two values and two gradients for a product derivative. The existing logarithmic tangent formula p16-q12 and symbolic product tasks do not require these respective graph-to-bound or graph-product decisions. Teaching and prior graph knowledge establish eligibility, not exam representation.

reviews.scope: Whole multiple-choice task and four options; original image personally viewed and native TikZ inspected.
reviews.minimumSelection: selected: global tangent comparison on the specified cosine lobe is not the local coefficient bounds task.
reviews.derivation: The diagram selects 3π/2<a<2π. Tangency through the origin gives m=cos(a)/a, and 0<cos(a)<1 gives m<1/a. Strict concavity on (3π/2,5π/2) puts the tangent strictly above cos x at 2π, hence 2πm>1. Thus 1/(2π)<m<1/a, option B. The given worked and short answers agree.
reviews.sourceFidelity: Prompt and all options retained, source marks omitted. Viewed source shows the first positive lobe, origin tangent, a projection and ±1; native cosine and tangent satisfy the same relations, including the selected lobe. Origin label O is omitted under the standing convention. Native dimensions and final print appearance were not inspected.

skillIds.assessment: Suitable: tangent gradient and cosine shape/derivatives support the comparison.

reviews.difficultyReason: The decisive unsignposted comparison is to evaluate the tangent against the cosine maximum at a different x-value on the correct lobe; the other bound follows from the tangency point.

reviews.scope: Whole multiple-choice task and four options; original image personally viewed and native TikZ inspected.
reviews.minimumSelection: selected: interval-to-gradient and intercept bounds are a different local demand from cosine global tangent comparison.
reviews.derivation: The graph places 1<a<e. At tangency m=1/a, so 1/e<m<1. Substitution of (a,ln a) gives c=ln a−1, and 0<ln a<1 gives −1<c<0. Only A satisfies both; short and worked answers agree.
reviews.sourceFidelity: All options and graph givens are retained; marks and origin O omitted by convention. The source wording says the tangent is shown, but the personally viewed original shows no tangent; the native graph correctly preserves this source fault without adding a line. The text states tangency and the graph supplies the interval, so the problem is mathematically determinate. Native dimensions and final print appearance were not inspected.

reviews.difficultyReason: Translate a graphical interval into strict bounds for two different coefficients, deriving the intercept from a symbolic point and tangent gradient.

reviews.scope: Whole multipart task, parts a and b; original image personally viewed and native TikZ inspected.
reviews.minimumSelection: selected: transformation recognition followed by graph values and slopes in a product rule is not represented by the two tangent-bound questions or symbolic product practice.
reviews.derivation: The two line segments of f have slopes 1/2 and −3, vertex (4,6); those of g have slopes −3 and 1/2, vertex (3,0). Reflecting in the y-axis, translating right 7, reflecting in the x-axis and translating up 6 gives g(x)=6−f(7−x), matching the shown rays. At x=1, f=4.5, f′=1/2, g=6 and g′=−3; therefore u′(1)=(1/2)(6)+4.5(−3)=−10.5. Both source answers are correct; x=1 is away from the corners.
reviews.sourceFidelity: Viewed source and native preserve graph vertices, values, slopes, distinct dash patterns, grid, axis numbering, continuation arrows, both parts and transformation condition; marks omitted. The construction supplies no extra printed coordinates or solution. Native dimensions and final print appearance were not inspected.

reviews.difficultyReason: Infer a multi-step transformation from corresponding piecewise-linear graphs, then independently extract two function values and two signed gradients and combine them with the product rule.

Ordinary prior graph transformations, line gradients, coordinate reading and logarithm/cosine graphs support eligibility. These examples are not a substitute for the distinct exam demands.
